AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #15
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why should you wear gloves when handling compost materials? (1 mark)
   A. To keep your hands cold
   B. To make the compost sweeter
   C. So the heap grows faster
   D. To protect your hands from dirt and germs

2. What is the purpose of sticks at the bottom of the compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. They make it look neat
   B. They keep the heap dry forever
   C. They let air move through the heap
   D. They add plant food

3. How can you tell that a plant has enough water? (1 mark)
   A. The pot is empty
   B. The soil is damp about a finger deep
   C. The leaves are gone
   D. The soil is dust

4. What should you do with the fire when cooking is finished? (1 mark)
   A. Put it out
   B. Leave it burning
   C. Add more wood
   D. Pour paraffin on it

5. Why do children need an adult when cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Fire is not dangerous
   B. Fuels and fire can burn people
   C. Children cannot lift a spoon
   D. Adults always cook faster

6. Why do we use more than one method of scaring animals? (1 mark)
   A. Animals can get used to one method
   B. One method is always cheaper
   C. It uses more soil
   D. It confuses farmers

7. Why do we label the seedbed rows? (1 mark)
   A. To remember the crop and the date sown
   B. To scare birds
   C. To give plants names
   D. To decorate

8. How can a person without a garden grow tiny-seeded crops? (1 mark)
   A. On hard rock
   B. In a container seedbed with drainage holes
   C. On a road
   D. Only in a forest

9. Which is an example of caring for fruit plants? (1 mark)
   A. Burning the leaves
   B. Leaving them without water
   C. Cutting the roots
   D. Watering, weeding and mulching

10. Which practice keeps children safe when harvesting fruit? (1 mark)
   A. Push each other
   B. Use a picking pole and take turns
   C. Climb all trees
   D. Pull the branch down hard

11. Which site is suitable for planting a fruit tree? (1 mark)
   A. Inside a building
   B. A deep shade under big trees
   C. A flooded area
   D. A sunny place with space to spread

12. Why is a hole dug before planting a tree seedling? (1 mark)
   A. To give the tree shade
   B. To hide the seedling
   C. To water the neighbours
   D. To loosen the soil so roots can grow easily

13. What can an agricultural extension officer help with? (1 mark)
   A. Building a house
   B. Advice on which varieties and methods suit your area
   C. Cooking meals
   D. Selling your tools

14. About how big should a planting hole for a fruit tree be? (1 mark)
   A. 10 cm wide only
   B. About 1 cm
   C. As big as a football field
   D. About half a metre wide and deep

15. Which of these can oxen do on a farm? (1 mark)
   A. Lay eggs
   B. Give wool
   C. Pull ploughs and carts
   D. Produce honey

16. Which of these is an animal welfare need? (1 mark)
   A. No shelter
   B. Being hit
   C. Clean water always available
   D. Living in mud

17. What is a male sheep called? (1 mark)
   A. Cock
   B. Ram
   C. Bull
   D. Billy

18. Which of these is a domestic animal? (1 mark)
   A. Zebra
   B. Lion
   C. Giraffe
   D. Goat

19. Which domestic animal is often kept in dry areas for milk and meat? (1 mark)
   A. Pig
   B. Camel
   C. Duck
   D. Rabbit

20. Which fruit is a protective food? (1 mark)
   A. Chapati
   B. Rice
   C. Ugali
   D. Mango

21. Which group does githeri belong to mainly? (1 mark)
   A. Drinks
   B. Energy and body-building
   C. Only protective
   D. Only water

22. Which meal is missing protective foods? (1 mark)
   A. Sweet potato, egg and spinach
   B. Githeri and avocado
   C. Ugali, beans and cabbage
   D. Rice and fish only

23. What is a balanced meal? (1 mark)
   A. A meal with foods from all the main groups in the right amounts
   B. A meal of only sweets
   C. A very large meal
   D. A meal with only one kind of food

24. Which is an advantage of boiling? (1 mark)
   A. It needs no oil
   B. It always burns food
   C. It makes food black
   D. It needs deep oil

25. What should you do first for a small burn? (1 mark)
   A. Cover with toothpaste
   B. Put butter on it
   C. Ignore it
   D. Cool it under running clean water for at least ten minutes

26. What is shallow frying? (1 mark)
   A. Cooking in a lot of deep oil
   B. Cooking in a small amount of hot oil in a pan
   C. Cooking in water
   D. Baking in an oven

27. Why do we cook food? (1 mark)
   A. To make it colder
   B. To make it dirty
   C. To make it soft, tasty and safe to eat
   D. To make it disappear

28. Why should fingernails be kept short? (1 mark)
   A. Nails are food
   B. Germs and worm eggs hide under long nails
   C. Short nails grow faster
   D. Long nails are heavy

29. Which disease can result from drinking unsafe water? (1 mark)
   A. Toothache
   B. Cholera
   C. Sunburn
   D. A cut

30. Which part is often forgotten when washing hands? (1 mark)
   A. The elbows only
   B. Under the nails and between the fingers
   C. Only the palms
   D. The knees

31. Which food is bad for teeth if eaten too often? (1 mark)
   A. Vegetables
   B. Water
   C. Sweets
   D. Eggs

32. What is the use of a hygiene log? (1 mark)
   A. Measuring rain
   B. Listing games
   C. Recording daily hygiene practices
   D. Counting money

33. Why should food be covered in the kitchen? (1 mark)
   A. To make it heavier
   B. To hide the plate
   C. To keep off flies, rats and cockroaches
   D. To keep it hot forever

34. Why should the compound be free of long grass and rubbish? (1 mark)
   A. It looks colourful
   B. To stop rain
   C. Snakes, rats and mosquitoes can hide there
   D. To save soap

35. Which is the correct order for washing dishes? (1 mark)
   A. Least greasy first, greasy last
   B. Rinse only with soap
   C. Any order in dirty water
   D. Greasy first

36. About how long is the long stitch in long and short tacking? (1 mark)
   A. 20 cm
   B. 2 mm
   C. 2 cm
   D. 2 metres

37. What size square did we cut for the handkerchief? (1 mark)
   A. 1 m by 1 m
   B. 25 cm by 25 cm
   C. 2 cm by 2 cm
   D. 5 m by 5 m

38. What is a pin cushion used for? (1 mark)
   A. Ironing cloth
   B. Keeping needles and pins safe
   C. Cutting cloth
   D. Measuring cloth

39. Which is a mistake in tacking? (1 mark)
   A. Marking the line first
   B. Using small back stitch at the end
   C. Making stitches of different lengths in even tacking
   D. Using contrasting thread

40. What do you use to mark a straight line on cloth? (1 mark)
   A. A broom
   B. Chalk and a ruler
   C. A plate
   D. A hammer

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Give three good personal hygiene practices apart from washing hands. (3 marks)

42. List four safety rules when cooking. (4 marks)

43. Write the steps for preparing a meal using both boiling and shallow frying. Include hygiene and safety. (5 marks)

44. Give three reasons why nails should be kept short and clean. (3 marks)

45. Describe how to prepare a class talk about one domestic animal. (4 marks)

46. Describe how to care for a seedbed after sowing. (4 marks)

47. Give three ways of saving fuel when cooking. (3 marks)

48. Describe how to make a simple trellis for passion fruit. (4 marks)

49. Name two things that should never be put in a compost heap and say why. (2 marks)

50. Plan a balanced supper using local foods and name the group of each food. (3 marks)

51. Give three peaceful ways of protecting crops from birds and animals apart from a scarecrow. (3 marks)

52. How can you tell that compost is ready for use? (3 marks)

53. Explain why we must not leave a fire burning after cooking. (2 marks)

54. Explain what a fruit is in plant growth. (2 marks)

55. Why should tiny seeds be sown shallowly? (2 marks)

56. What should be done with a paper dust mask that is dirty? (2 marks)

57. Describe the first aid for a small burn. (3 marks)

58. Give three benefits of using compost manure on the farm. (3 marks)

59. Explain how to make a meal of boiled potatoes and fried egg balanced. (3 marks)

60. Name two materials that can be used to make compost. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #15 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — To protect your hands from dirt and germs
   Gloves protect against germs and cuts.

2. C — They let air move through the heap
   Air helps the tiny living things rot the wastes.

3. B — The soil is damp about a finger deep
   Feeling the soil shows if the roots have water.

4. A — Put it out
   Leaving fire burning wastes fuel and is dangerous.

5. B — Fuels and fire can burn people
   Adults can guide and help prevent accidents.

6. A — Animals can get used to one method
   A mix of methods works better.

7. A — To remember the crop and the date sown
   Labels prevent confusion.

8. B — In a container seedbed with drainage holes
   A box or tin with holes and fine soil works well.

9. D — Watering, weeding and mulching
   Care keeps plants healthy.

10. B — Use a picking pole and take turns
   Use safe methods.

11. D — A sunny place with space to spread
   Fruit trees need light and space.

12. D — To loosen the soil so roots can grow easily
   Loose soil lets roots spread.

13. B — Advice on which varieties and methods suit your area
   Extension officers advise farmers.

14. D — About half a metre wide and deep
   The hole gives roots space in loose soil.

15. C — Pull ploughs and carts
   Oxen give draught power.

16. C — Clean water always available
   Animals need water, feed, shelter, health care and kind treatment.

17. B — Ram
   A ram is a male sheep.

18. D — Goat
   Goats are kept by farmers.

19. B — Camel
   Camels survive in dry regions.

20. D — Mango
   Mango has vitamins.

21. B — Energy and body-building
   Maize gives energy, beans give protein.

22. D — Rice and fish only
   Rice and fish have energy and protein but no vegetables or fruits.

23. A — A meal with foods from all the main groups in the right amounts
   A balanced meal includes energy, body-building and protective foods.

24. A — It needs no oil
   Boiled food is low in fat.

25. D — Cool it under running clean water for at least ten minutes
   Cooling reduces burn damage.

26. B — Cooking in a small amount of hot oil in a pan
   Shallow frying uses a thin layer of oil.

27. C — To make it soft, tasty and safe to eat
   Heat kills germs and softens food.

28. B — Germs and worm eggs hide under long nails
   Clean short nails prevent infection.

29. B — Cholera
   Cholera spreads through dirty water.

30. B — Under the nails and between the fingers
   Germs hide there.

31. C — Sweets
   Sugar helps decay.

32. C — Recording daily hygiene practices
   A log helps to form habits.

33. C — To keep off flies, rats and cockroaches
   Covered food is protected.

34. C — Snakes, rats and mosquitoes can hide there
   A tidy compound is safer.

35. A — Least greasy first, greasy last
   Water stays cleaner longer.

36. C — 2 cm
   The long stitch is about 2 cm.

37. B — 25 cm by 25 cm
   A small handkerchief is easy to make.

38. B — Keeping needles and pins safe
   It holds sharp objects.

39. C — Making stitches of different lengths in even tacking
   Stitches should be equal.

40. B — Chalk and a ruler
   Chalk marks show the line.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Bathing daily, brushing teeth twice a day, keeping nails short, wearing clean clothes, drinking safe water (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Cook with an adult; turn handles inward; use a dry cloth for hot pots; open lids away from the face; keep water away from hot oil (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: Wash hands; wash food; boil potatoes until soft; shallow fry an egg or fish; serve with vegetables; safety: adult present, handles inward, dry cloth, water away from hot oil; clean up after.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for hygiene, 1 for boiling, 1 for frying, 1 for safety, 1 for serving and cleaning.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Germs hide under nails, worm eggs are found there, and long nails can scratch and cause injury.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose an animal; collect pictures; list its uses and care; practise speaking clearly; present and answer questions.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Water gently and regularly, remove weeds, thin the seedlings, and protect the bed from animals and birds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct activity.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use a lid on the pot, cut food small, use dry firewood, put out the fire after cooking, soak beans first, or use an improved jiko (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Fix strong posts about 2 m tall; tie strong wires or strings between them; plant seedlings near the posts; tie the stems gently to the wires.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: Plastic and glass, because they do not rot.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two items, 1 mark for the reason.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example, rice (energy), fish (body-building), spinach (protective).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each food correctly named and placed.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Nets, fences, noise makers, shiny objects, guarding at the time animals come (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each method.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is dark brown, crumbly, smells like earth, and the original wastes cannot be seen.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sign.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: It wastes fuel and can cause a fire or accident.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for waste, 1 mark for danger.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: The part of a plant that holds the seeds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for part of a plant, 1 mark for holding seeds.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: They have little stored food so they cannot push up through deep soil.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for little food, 1 mark for not reaching the surface.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is thrown away and replaced, not washed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for throwing, 1 mark for replacing.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put the burn under cool running clean water for at least ten minutes, cover it loosely with a clean cloth and tell an adult.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: It feeds crops, it softens the soil and helps it to hold water, and it is cheap because it uses waste.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct benefit.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: Potatoes give energy and the egg gives protein. Add vegetables such as spinach or tomato for protective foods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each group named.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: Vegetable peelings, dry leaves, grass, straw or animal dung (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct material.
